method: viral-reverse-engineering skill. Public page metadata read in the built-in browser (views, length, channel, publish date, likes). Frames: 2 to 3 screenshots per video only; no full watch, no audio, no comment sampling. Sample is small and relevance-ranked, not a ranked top list.
ethics: Patterns only. Do not copy footage, characters, scripts or channel branding. All app output stays original.

sample.note: Real person in a bright red uniform dress, handheld follow shot from behind, bystanders turn to look.
observed: opens on her back, centre frame, moving
bystanders visibly react (head turns) which proves she stands out
title promises an effect on other people
sample.driver: Social proof: other people's reactions show she stands out, instead of telling the viewer she does.
sample.replicable: partly (real-world reaction footage, creator's own audience, unknown account size)

sample.note: Lone woman walking on a road; title and caption pose a worry ('must be lost').
observed: title is a question-in-image: why is she there
sample.driver: Curiosity gap from one oddly placed figure; the viewer wants the explanation.
sample.replicable: yes as mechanism; unknown account size

sample.note: AI short film made with a hosted tool; caption states a betrayal premise in one line.
observed: one concrete physical beat (hand under table)
sample.driver: One clear stakes line plus one concrete action.
sample.replicable: yes as structure; production quality is hosted-model quality, not local

sample.note: 10 s mythic spectacle made with a hosted model; promoted as an experiment.
sample.driver: Spectacle plus novelty of the tool.

sample.note: 9 s food Short; title is a craving promise.
sample.driver: Craving plus very short length (likely high completion).
Aesthetic only; no share trigger visible.

findings: Realistic night-walk cinematic Shorts in this sample mostly stay at 1 to 70 thousand views; the red-dress video with 2.6 million views shows other people reacting to her.
Her back or profile leads the frame in the stand-out example, which matches the identity-safe angle the local model needs.
Short length (9 to 22 s) dominates the high-view food sample; the walking sample ranges 7 to 40 s.
AI films that did well state one premise sentence and show one concrete physical beat.
Large-account effect is unmeasured: channel size was not captured, so none of these is proven replicable.
appRules: Show the stand-out effect through others' reactions (turning heads) when the model can render it; otherwise through one clear light cue, and flag it as weaker.
Open on a moving back or profile of the main subject, centre frame, within the first second.
State one premise sentence in the title or on-screen text; make one concrete physical beat visible.
Keep 10 to 20 s unless the story needs more.
Mark crowd reactions as yellow/red risk for the local motion model: render a test first.
